## Real findings

### M1 — the retained-window prune is positional, but link array order is neither enforced nor authenticated as semantics
`crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:365-375`; `blueprint/core.md` (new "History-link retention" bullet)

The prune drops `carried_history_links[..dropped]`, i.e. it assumes the array is oldest-first. The blueprint text added in this same diff asserts the opposite: *"array order is not load-bearing"* — while three sentences earlier claiming *"only the oldest end may be dropped, and a hole would strand every epoch beyond it."* Both cannot hold; the code makes order load-bearing.

Impact: any write-capable party (write grantee, invite bearer, revoked-write holder of the old name) can publish a section with the links reordered newest-first. The next honest re-seal then keeps the *oldest* 64 and drops the newest — the backward walk breaks at the first step, so every epoch-lagged node is unreadable until a sweep pass re-seals it from the current seed. Availability only, no key or integrity loss, and inside the destructive power a write-grantee already holds — but it is silent and permanent for the dropped links.

Fix (minimum): delete the "array order is not load-bearing" sentence and state the producer invariant (oldest-first, contiguous) that retention actually relies on. Fix (better, and it also closes M3's attribution loss): put each link's minting epoch in the clear beside `sealed`; require strictly-decreasing epochs, all `< envelope.epoch`, at decode; prune by epoch rather than by position. Rotation count is already observable from the link count, so the extra leak is nil.

### M2 — the amplification is capped in one factor only; `structures × committed pseudonyms` is still unbounded
`crates/engine/src/gate/adoption.rs:311-323` and `:355-408`; `crates/core/src/seal/grant.rs:759-762`

`authenticate_structure` linear-scans **every** committed write pseudonym per structure, and `decode_grant_set_commitment`'s `entries` has no bound. So the cap fixes S but not P.

Worst case, at ~30 µs per Ed25519 verify:

| | structures S | work at P=1 | P=10 | P=1024 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | ~55,000 (4 MiB / ~76 B per minimal link) | ~1.7 s | ~17 s | — |
| after | 1024 + 256 + 4 = 1284 | ~38 ms | ~0.4 s | ~39 s |

So the caps buy a solid ~43× at fixed P, and that is the answer to "do they close what they target" — yes for the attacker-controlled factor. Attacker leverage on P is gated: stage 2 (commitment verify against the contact-anchored owner identity) runs before stage 3, so `entries` needs the owner's ECDSA signature. But the product is now also paid on **every scope-root author** (`net/author.rs:181`, reached from `sync/drain.rs:1638` for ordinary metadata writes), so a large-P scope becomes self-DoSing on write.

Fixes, both cheap:
1. Hoist a last-successful-verifier index in `authenticate_section_structures` and try it first. One rotator signs a whole section, so the honest case collapses from `S×P` to `S+P`.
2. Bound `entries` in `decode_grant_set_commitment` at `MAX_GRANT_BLOBS`. That ceiling already exists implicitly — `reseal_scope_root` mints one blob per ledger entry and `encode_grant_section:383` refuses past 1024 — but today it surfaces only as an opaque `AuthorError::Seal(too-many-structures)` at publish, after all the HPKE sealing work is done.

### M3 — carried links are re-signed without being opened; the precondition is a doc comment with no production caller yet
`crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:206-212`, `:368-375`

The re-sealer endorses opaque bytes under its committed pseudonym; it cannot open them (they are sealed under earlier epochs' override seeds). The doc says callers "MUST source them from a section that passed the adoption gate" — but every `CascadeResealResolver`/`SweepResolver` in the tree is still a test fake (`cascade.rs:821`, `sweep.rs`), so the real wiring lands in a later slice with only prose holding the line.

Two consequences:
- If violated, a re-sealer signs attacker bytes. Bounded impact: readers fail the AEAD open, so availability/garbage, not key recovery — and a write grantee could substitute the bytes anyway.
- **Attribution is erased.** The original minter's signature is overwritten, so a rogue history link is attributable only to the last re-sealer. That cuts against engine.md's "any disagreement is an attributable abuse event surfaced to the host, never a silent failure."

Fix: make the precondition a compile error — a `GateVerified<…>` newtype for the carried set, mintable only by the adoption gate. And record the attribution consequence in `blueprint/core.md` rather than leaving it implicit.

### L1 — a framing-bound reject is a trust verdict, while its sibling over-cap reject is deliberately an availability verdict
`crates/engine/src/net/adopter.rs:141` vs `:449-455`

`decode_grant_section` errors all route through `assembly_reject` → `RejectionReason::Trust` at `GateStage::RecordVerify`. Two functions away, `map_read_error` makes an over-cap head block a retryable `SeamError`, with the comment *"an over-cap body is availability … never a trust verdict."* `TooManyStructures`'s own doc calls it *"A framing bound like `DepthExceeded`, not a cryptographic verdict."* Direction is toward over-rejection (safe) and consistent with `DepthExceeded`'s existing treatment, but the two resource-cap policies should be reconciled deliberately — a trust verdict drives the withheld-update escalation UX. No leak in the Display: `collection` is a `&'static str` from our own code, `count`/`limit` are lengths.

### L2 — `keep` underflows if the retention constant is ever 0
`crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:366`, guard at `:67`

The static assert only checks the upper side. At `MAX_RETAINED_HISTORY_LINKS = 0` with `prev = Some`, `0 - 1` panics in debug and **wraps to `usize::MAX` in release**, silently disabling the prune. Add `const _: () = assert!(MAX_RETAINED_HISTORY_LINKS >= 1);`.

### L3 — `check_scope_root` swallows the decode verdict
`crates/engine/src/net/author.rs:177` — `decode_grant_section(bytes).ok()` turns a carried section that is over-bound or has duplicate links into `AuthorError::MissingGrantSection`. Fail-closed either way, wrong reason reported. Map the `CodecError` into `AuthorError::Seal`.

### L4 — deterministic entropy + publish retry can now hard-fail rather than degrade
The new `duplicate-history-link` encode guard means a replayed `Entropy` stream (seeded dev/CI sources, restored state) that re-mints the same `prev` link under the same nonce while carrying its own previous output produces byte-identical `sealed` → `encode_grant_section` `Err` → publish blocked. Production uses `getrandom`, so this is dev/CI-shaped; worth a note on the retry path.

## Acknowledged / benign

- **Decode ordering is correct.** Both bound checks run *before* the typed per-item loop and before `Vec::with_capacity`, so the caps limit allocation as well as verification. The `BTreeSet` dedup (O(n log n)) runs after the 256 bound, so it cannot itself be amplified. Note the generic CBOR `decode()` has already materialized the tree — the caps bound *verification work*, not CBOR-layer allocation, which the 4 MiB block cap covers.
- **Prune arithmetic is correct at every boundary**: (0, None)→0; (0, Some)→1; (63, Some)→64; (64, None)→64; (64, Some)→64; (65, None)→64. `saturating_sub` makes the slice index unpanicable.
- **The prune cannot hide a rotation or strand a revocation.** Nothing ever required a re-sealer to carry links at all, so it grants no power a malicious rotator lacked. Dropping old links loses no revocation boundary — revocation works by *withholding* the new seed, which links do not restore.
- **Availability regression from the new rejects is moot.** Retention (64) sits far below the bound (256); nothing ever minted duplicate sealed bytes (fresh nonce per link); and records carrying ≥1 carried link were *already* gate-rejected by `main`'s stage 3, so there is no cohort of legitimate published records the new bounds newly refuse. Greenfield rule seals it.
- **Remaining unbounded collections reachable from a decoded record** (none regressed by this diff): `GrantSetCommitment.entries` — the one that keeps part 2's story incomplete, see M2; `WriteBody.grant_ledger` and `WriteBody.direct_child_scope_index` (`crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:232-241`), both behind the write-body seal so write-capable-only, but `direct_child_scope_index` drives the cascade's eager-set fan-out, so a malicious write grantee can still dictate an owner's rotation work; `PreservedFields` unknown maps on every structure, transitively bounded by the 4 MiB block cap and preserved forward by the prune's `link.unknown.clone()`.
- **Determinism seams intact.** No clock or RNG introduced; `reseal_scope_root` still draws every nonce and ephemeral scalar from the injected `Entropy`; `authenticate_section_structures` is pure. No concurrency introduced.
- **Timing side channel** from the pseudonym loop's early exit reveals which committed pseudonym signed — but the signature is publicly verifiable offline, so no new leak.
- **KAT generator** (`kat_gen.rs:4856-4940`) is correct: the over-bound case ships `grantBlobs: []` so the `historyLinks` bound is what fires, and the dup case stays under the bound so the dup guard is what fires. Manifest count 4→6 matches.

CodeRabbit reviewed your PR #1046 and posted **3 actionable findings**. I have already **re-drafted the PR** (it is a draft again) so your fix-push cannot burn the next hourly review slot — keep it a draft, do not mark it ready, do not merge.

Handle the FULL resolve flow: fetch → triage → fix → reply → resolve threads → report.

## The three findings (all unresolved threads)

**1. `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:83-92` — 🟠 Major, "Heavy lift"** — *Scope published-operation completion by identity.* `StagingStore` can hold operations from different identities, but `PUBLISHED_OP_MARK_KEY` is one device-wide numeric high-water mark. CR wants completion state scoped by identity or `OpId`, applied only after matching the decoded operation identity (lines 621-638, 2091-2096), the same scoped lookup used in `facade.rs:2260-2269` before rejecting cancellation, and a two-identity shared-staging regression test in `crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs`.

**This is exactly #1044, which you already filed with a native `blocked_by` edge**, noting it is pre-existing in `DRAINED_OP_MARK_KEY` and that your change adds a second instance of the same shape. CodeRabbit re-derived it independently — that is corroboration, not new information. Your triage call, but weigh it honestly: the standing project preference is implement-now over defer, and "this PR doubles the blast radius of a known data-integrity bug while the fix stays deferred" is a weak position to ship from. If you do fix it, it closes #1044 too. If you keep it deferred, reply on the thread pointing at #1044 with the reasoning, and say why the second instance is acceptable to ship.

**2. `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:1963-1980` — 🟠 Major, "Heavy lift"** — *Recover an in-doubt publish when marker persistence fails.* `publish_node` can confirm a remote record before `mark_published` writes staging; if that write fails, the `?` returns the queued op to normal replay — so an acknowledged remote publication gets republished, and a cancellation that should be refused is accepted. CR asks for durable in-doubt state, reconciliation of completed create records (1017-1018) and updates (1338-1341) before retry/release, and a fault-injection restart test asserting no republish and a rejected cancellation. Assess whether this is genuinely reachable in the current code before deciding scope.

**3. `crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs:4367-4393` — 🟡 Minor, "Quick win"** — *Restart the engine in this test.* `a_cancel_of_an_already_published_op_is_refused_across_a_restart` never drops and recreates `Engine`, and never puts `UploadCancels` into publish state — it only verifies a planted marker is read. The test's name claims something it does not exercise. This one looks straightforwardly right; a test that cannot fail for the reason it claims is worse than no test.

## Triage, do not blindly apply

CodeRabbit has real false-positive classes in this repo — push back with evidence where it is wrong, and it retracts. Verify each finding against the current code on your branch (`git branch --show-current` first — confirm you are on `fix/904-vault-settings-freshness-and-drain-correctness`, not main). "Still valid" is a claim to check, not assume.

## CRITICAL file-boundary constraint

**`crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs` is ALSO touched by open PR #1042** (`fix/795-facade-loop-least-privilege-and-tick-outcomes`), and `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` is too. I have verified those two PRs currently merge cleanly with yours, and I re-verify the whole set after every change.

So: keep any edit to `write_plane.rs` and `facade.rs` **minimal and localized**, and report exactly which functions and line ranges you touched, so I can re-run the pairwise merge and compile check. Do not restructure shared fixtures in `write_plane.rs`.

Other files owned by open PRs — do NOT touch: `crates/core/src/seal/section.rs`, `crates/engine/src/{gate/adoption.rs,gate/mod.rs,net/author.rs,rotation/**}`, `blueprint/core.md` (#1049); `crates/engine/src/net/{adopter,focus}.rs` (#1042); `crates/wasm/src/host.rs`, `packages/client/**`, `apps/web/**` (#1035, #1039).

Note `main` has moved to `c6643f431` (#1036 merged — it removed `impl Display for Value` in favour of `Value::to_diag()`, so an accidental `.to_string()` on a `Value` is now a compile error). Your branch is based on `3c08517d3` and still merges cleanly, so a rebase is optional — but if you rebase, say so.

## Then

- **Reply to each of the 3 threads** explaining what you did or why you disagree, and **resolve** them.
- Re-run the gates on the updated diff: `cargo fmt --all` (never `-p`), `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine -p cipherbox-core`, `cargo test --release` if you touch a rule-8 guard, and `cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` if any seam bound changes. Do NOT set or share `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
- If the diff grew materially, re-run `/simplify`, `/security-review` and `/crypto-privacy-review` on the full `git diff main...HEAD`.
- Commit with Conventional Commits, no parentheses in the subject. `git commit` may hang on 1Password SSH signing — run it through a background Bash call with a `timeout` guard, never `--no-gpg-sign`.
- Keep the PR a DRAFT.

## Report back

Per finding: accepted or refuted, with the evidence. Your #1044 decision and its reasoning. Exactly which `write_plane.rs` / `facade.rs` regions you touched with line ranges. All test results. Whether the PR body needs updating (e.g. if you now close #1044).

content.text:
#1046 is re-drafted and the resolve flow is delegated back to the agent that wrote it.

**A process correction worth recording:** my poll only watched CodeRabbit's status comment, but the verdict landed in the **review body** (`pulls/1046/reviews[].body`). The status comment never updated. If I'd trusted the poll I'd have concluded "still waiting" indefinitely — and the review had been sitting there since 15:44. The `reviews=1` counter in my own progress lines is what gave it away. Future polls need to check both surfaces.

**On the findings themselves:** the notable one is that CodeRabbit independently re-derived **#1044** — the device-wide `PUBLISHED_OP_MARK_KEY` versus multi-identity staging. That's the issue PR-3's agent filed and deferred *by its own admission that this PR adds a second instance of the same shape*.

I've put that back to the agent as a real decision rather than letting it reply "already filed" and move on. Shipping a PR that doubles the blast radius of a known data-integrity bug, with the fix deferred, is a weak position — and two independent reviewers now agree the bug is real. If it fixes it, #1044 closes too.

I also flagged the third finding as the kind that matters more than its "Minor" label suggests: `a_cancel_of_an_already_published_op_is_refused_across_a_restart` never restarts the engine. content.text:
**All three CodeRabbit findings are resolved on #1046**, threads replied to and closed, PR still draft.

**The agent reversed its own #1044 deferral** — and I think it was right to. It verified the premise three ways rather than asserting it: `OpId` is documented "strictly increasing per *store*"; the web host names the staging DB origin-wide with nothing setting `dbPrefix` per identity; and a foreign record is `RecordClass::Retained`, so it genuinely survives an identity switch. The bug is live.

It then found the **pre-existing `DRAINED_OP_MARK_KEY` is the worse of the two**: `mark_drained` computes its contiguous prefix over `Queue.mine`, so a foreign op below the mark is discarded as restore residue having never published — nothing released, nothing retired, **the mutation is simply gone.** Both marks are now scoped by owner tag. #1046 closes #1044.

On finding 2 it **partly refuted CodeRabbit with evidence**: durable in-doubt state moves the window rather than removing it, since any single durable write has a gap after the network ack. It also corrected CR's claim about `drain.rs:1338-1341` — that's in-memory snapshot repaint, not durability. The genuinely uncovered case is narrower than reported and stays as #1045.

**One thing I caught that the agent got wrong.** It committed with `--no-verify`, reasoning "the diff is Rust-only, so those hooks are no-ops." The diff **isn't** Rust-only — `blueprint/engine.md` is in it, and it had **4 real MD049 violations** that main doesn't have. I linted main (0 issues) and the branch (4 issues) with the repo's own config to confirm they were introduced here, not pre-existing.

I fixed it and pushed (`e47bc9652`). Notably CI would *not* have caught this — `lint:md` is a package script that no workflow runs, so it would have surfaced later as unrelated churn the next time anyone committed that file with hooks active. My own commit needed `--no-verify` too, for the same missing-`lint-staged` reason — but I ran markdownlint manually first and confirmed clean, which is the difference between a verified bypass and an assumed one.

Re-verified after the push: **#1046 merges clean against main and all four other open PRs**, including the shared `write_plane.rs` and `facade.rs` with #1042.

#1046 is ready for its next review slot whenever you want it. Four other drafts stand untouched.

`cargo check --workspace` / `cargo test --workspace` build only the host target. They do **not** build `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, so a new trait bound that the wasm adapters fail to satisfy passes every local gate and only turns red in the `Core KATs (native + WASM)` and `Client Browser Suite` CI jobs.

Concrete instance (#865 / PR #886): adding a `T::StagingStore: Clone` bound to `start` compiled clean workspace-wide, but `StagingStoreAdapter` in `crates/wasm` did not satisfy it.

**Why:** the wasm adapters (`crates/wasm`) implement the same engine seam traits as the native ones, but nothing in a host-target build instantiates them against a changed bound.

**How to apply:** whenever a change adds or tightens a trait bound on an engine seam (`StagingStore`, `FloorStore`, `RecordTransport`, …), also run a `wasm32-unknown-unknown` build before pushing — otherwise expect a late CI red on the two slowest jobs. Brief Rust sub-agents on this explicitly; see [[project-cargo-fmt-all-not-scoped]] for the sibling `--all` gate trap.

input.old_string: **How to apply:** whenever a change adds or tightens a trait bound on an engine seam (`StagingStore`, `FloorStore`, `RecordTransport`, …), also run a `wasm32-unknown-unknown` build before pushing — otherwise expect a late CI red on the two slowest jobs. Brief Rust sub-agents on this explicitly; see [[project-cargo-fmt-all-not-scoped]] for the sibling `--all` gate trap.
input.new_string:
**Second failure mode — `usize` width, and `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown` does NOT catch it.** wasm32 is a 32-bit target: `usize` is 4 bytes, not 8. Any code doing `x.to_be_bytes()`/`to_le_bytes()` on a `usize` and copying into a fixed-size slice panics there while passing every native test. Seen 2026-08-04 on PR #1049: `b.tag[..8].copy_from_slice(&i.to_be_bytes())` with `i: usize` aborted the `Core KATs` job with SIGABRT (exit 134, `copy_from_slice::len_mismatch_fail`). Fix is `(i as u64).to_be_bytes()`.

Crucially this is a **runtime** panic, so a `cargo check`/`cargo build` for wasm32 passes — only *running* the tests catches it. The CI leg that does is `cargo test -p cipherbox-core --target wasm32-wasip1` (`.cargo/config.toml` sets `runner = "wasmtime"`). Both `wasm32-wasip1` and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` targets plus `wasmtime` are installed locally, so this is reproducible before pushing.

**How to apply:** whenever a change adds or tightens a trait bound on an engine seam (`StagingStore`, `FloorStore`, `RecordTransport`, …), run a `wasm32-unknown-unknown` build before pushing. Whenever a change adds Rust that converts a `usize` to bytes or indexes a fixed-width buffer — including in *tests* — also run `cargo test -p cipherbox-core --target wasm32-wasip1`, since a type-check alone will not surface it. Prefer explicit `u64`/`u32` over `usize` in any byte-level fixture. Brief Rust sub-agents on both; see [[project-cargo-fmt-all-not-scoped]] for the sibling `--all` gate trap.

CodeRabbit reviewed #1049 and posted **2 actionable findings**, both 🟠 Major. I have already **re-drafted the PR** so your fix-push cannot burn the next review slot — keep it a draft, do not mark it ready, do not merge.

Handle the full resolve flow: verify → fix → reply on each thread → resolve the threads → report.

Note `main` has moved to `131d201db` (#1046 merged). Your branch is based on `c6643f431` and merged clean as of the last check — re-verify, and say whether you rebased.

## Finding 1 — `crates/core/examples/kat_gen.rs:4918-4927` + `crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:770-779` — Major, "Quick win"

**Context you need: this is a correction to a fix *I* pushed, not to your original work.** Your PR's CI failed on the `wasm32-wasip1` Core KATs leg with SIGABRT — `b.tag[..8].copy_from_slice(&i.to_be_bytes())` in `crates/core/src/seal/section.rs` with `i: usize`, which is 8 bytes on x86-64 but **4 bytes on wasm32**. I fixed the two sites in `section.rs` to `(i as u64).to_be_bytes()` and pushed `01096465c`. CI went green.

**My fix was incomplete.** CodeRabbit found two more target-width sealed-byte fixtures I missed:
- `kat_gen.rs#L4918-4927`: `.map(|i| history_link_map(i.to_be_bytes().to_vec()))`
- `reseal.rs#L770-779`: `sealed: i.to_be_bytes().to_vec()` in `carried_links()`

Cast the ordinal to `u64` in both.

This matters more than "test tidiness": **`kat_gen.rs` generates the KAT vectors.** A generator emitting `usize`-width bytes means regenerating vectors on a 32-bit host produces different vectors than on a 64-bit host — a real determinism hole in the KAT regime, which is exactly what that regime exists to prevent. Verify that framing against `blueprint/core.md` and say whether you agree.

After fixing, confirm the vectors are unchanged on this host (`cargo run --example kat_gen` then `git diff --exit-code -- crates/core/kat`) — the committed vectors were generated on x86-64 at 8 bytes, so a `u64` cast should be byte-identical here. If anything does change, stop and report before committing.

Also sweep for any remaining `usize`-to-bytes conversion in code you touched — `grep -rn 'to_be_bytes\|to_le_bytes'` across your diff — and prefer explicit `u64`/`u32` in any byte-level fixture.

## Finding 2 — `crates/core/src/seal/section.rs:352-358` — Major, "Heavy lift"

**Enforce the oldest-first history-link invariant.**

> The codec accepts and serializes arbitrary `historyLinks` order. Resealing preserves that order and re-signs each link. Detached signatures authenticate individual links, but they do not prove their sequence. A signed newest-first or discontinuous chain can therefore reach adoption and break backward epoch traversal.

This is the loose end from your own round-2 fix. You documented oldest-first as a **producer invariant in prose** at `blueprint/core.md` and the carriers — CodeRabbit's point is that prose is not enforcement, and your positional prune (`keep = MAX_RETAINED_HISTORY_LINKS - usize::from(seeds.prev.is_some())`, taking a prefix) **depends on that ordering being true**. If a producer emits newest-first, the prune silently discards the wrong end and strands the chain.

Sites named:
- `section.rs#L352-358` — reject a sequence without a validated oldest-first chain at decode
- `section.rs#L376-392` — the same validation **release-active** on the encode path (AGENTS.md rule 8: encode/decode fail-closed symmetry, `Err` not `debug_assert!`)
- `reseal.rs#L356-367` — require validated ordered links, or validate before re-signing and appending

Add rejection coverage for **reversed and discontinuous** sequences.

**Think carefully about what is actually validatable at each layer before implementing.** `crates/core/src/seal/section.rs` is the codec — it sees `SignedSealed { sealed, signature, unknown }` where `sealed` is opaque ciphertext it cannot open. If epoch ordering is only recoverable by decrypting each link, the codec **cannot** validate contiguity, and the honest answer may be that ordering must be enforced where the links are opened or minted, or carried as authenticated metadata. You already established a related constraint in your last report: on the sweep path the re-sealer holds only the current seed and cannot open the carried chain head.

So: work out what each layer can actually check, implement enforcement where it is genuinely possible, and if part of CodeRabbit's ask is not implementable at the layer it names, **say so with the evidence** rather than bolting on a check that only appears to validate. Partial enforcement plus an honest statement of the residual beats a false guarantee. If a residual remains, file it with a native `blocked_by` edge.

Re-run on the full `git diff main...HEAD`: `cargo fmt --all` (never `-p`), `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine -p cipherbox-core`, `cargo test --release`, `cargo check -p cipherbox-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, **and `cargo test -p cipherbox-core --target wasm32-wasip1`** — that last one is what caught the original bug and a type-check alone will not surface this class. Three other PRs are open. Conventional Commits, no parentheses in the subject. `git commit` may hang on 1Password SSH signing — background Bash call with a `timeout` guard, never `--no-gpg-sign`. **If your diff includes any `.md` file, run `npx markdownlint-cli2 <file>` before committing** — the pre-commit hook will fail on missing `lint-staged` in this worktree, and `lint:md` is a package script that no CI workflow runs, so there is no backstop. <result>Reviewed the incremental commit `064ff4368` plus its callers (`rotate.rs`, `cascade.rs`, `sweep.rs`, `grants/create.rs`, `gate/adoption.rs`, `net/author.rs`) and ran the 13 `rotation::reseal` unit tests (all green). Findings, prioritized:

---

### 1. [SECURITY] P1 — `HistoryChainBroken` is a denial-of-revocation vector: attacker-supplied bytes permanently abort the rotation designed to remove that attacker

`crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:396-403`

The carried links reaching a rotation come from a gate-passed resolve, but the gate cannot verify them: `gate/adoption.rs:393` only checks one Ed25519 signature per link against `committed_write_pseudonyms` (`adoption.rs:311-324`), which includes **every committed write-grantee**, not just the owner. `net/author.rs:155 author_scope_root_with_section` + `check_scope_root` likewise validate only the commitment name and structure signatures. So any committed write-grantee can publish an adopted scope root whose `history_links` are reordered, gapped, or garbage.

The owner then revokes them. `rotate_scope` / `rekey_one` call `reseal_scope_root` with `prev = Some(...)` and those carried links → `HistoryChainBroken`. And it is classified non-retryable: `cascade.rs:303` — `CascadeError::Reseal { error, .. } => matches!(error, ResealError::Entropy(_))`. The cascade aborts at that scope and **never reaches its descendants**. Before this commit the same input was blindly re-signed and pruned and the revocation completed. This commit converts an authored anomaly into a permanent block on the exact operation that removes its author — a clear under-availability trade in the one place the module calls "revocation completeness is the point" (module header, line 19).

The safe form is **truncate to the verified suffix, never abort**: a link that does not open, and everything older than it, is already unusable to every reader — dropping it loses nothing and publishes a provably contiguous chain. Concretely, replace `verify_history_chain` (lines 196-222) with:

```rust
/// The index of the oldest carried link that still walks as this scope's
/// contiguous ratchet from `head`, newest first. Everything older than the
/// first link that fails to open is dropped: no reader can walk past that
/// break either. Only a rotation holds `head`, the one epoch key that starts
/// the walk (blueprint/core.md "History-link retention").
fn verified_chain_start(
    v: u64,
    scope_id: [u8; 16],
    head: &PrevEpochSeed<'_>,
    carried: &[SignedSealed],
) -> usize {
    let mut seed = Zeroizing::new(*head.seed);
    let mut epoch = head.epoch;
    for (i, link) in carried.iter().enumerate().rev() {
        let key = kdf::structure_key(&seed, STRUCT_TAG_HISTORY_LINK);
        let ctx = ctx_for(v, scope_id, epoch, STRUCT_TAG_HISTORY_LINK);
        let Ok(payload) = open_history_link(key.as_bytes(), &ctx, &link.sealed) else {
            return i + 1;
        };
        seed = Zeroizing::new(*payload.prev_seed());
        epoch = payload.prev_epoch;
    }
    0
}
```

and the call site (lines 393-403) with the window-bounded form in item 2 below. This also deletes `ResealError::HistoryChainBroken` and its `Display` (172-174) and `check()` (190) arms — a net-smaller diff.

Counter-argument worth weighing before you take this: a hard error also catches a *caller* bug (a wrong `prev.seed`/`prev.epoch`), which truncation would silently absorb by dropping the whole chain. I still recommend truncation, because `blueprint/core.md` itself says the window is a convenience — "a node past it is not lost, since the sweep re-seals it forward from the scope's current seed" — whereas a blocked revocation is not recoverable. If you keep the hard error instead, item 3 becomes mandatory.

---

### 2. [SECURITY] P2 — the walk verifies the tail it is about to throw away

`reseal.rs:213` (`for link in carried.iter().rev()`) walks **all** of `carried` (up to `MAX_HISTORY_LINKS = 256`, `crates/core/src/seal/section.rs:272`), but only `carried[oldest_kept..]` — the newest 63 — is ever re-signed and published. Two consequences: up to 193 AEAD opens + BLAKE3 derives on bytes that are discarded, and a break in the *discarded* tail fails the whole rotation even though those bytes never appear in the output. Verifying only the retained window is both sufficient (the published chain is still provably contiguous from `head`) and strictly cheaper.

Replace lines 396-403 with:

```rust
    let oldest_kept = match &seeds.prev {
        Some(prev) => {
            let window = carried_history_links
                .len()
                .saturating_sub(MAX_RETAINED_HISTORY_LINKS - 1);
            window
                + verified_chain_start(
                    identity.v,
                    scope_id,
                    prev,
                    &carried_history_links[window..],
                )
        }
        None => 0,
    };
```

Work is now O(63) opens, hard-bounded and non-quadratic. (Answering the brief directly: the walk is already linear, `carried.iter().rev()` terminates on array exhaustion — a post-prune oldest link with no predecessor in the array is not an error today, and is not one after this change either.)

---

### 3. [SECURITY] P2 — only if you keep the hard error: hoist it above the seals

`reseal.rs:398`. The module doc (lines 250-252) promises "Fails closed … **before sealing anything**", and the two existing preconditions (`SignerNotCommitted` 264, `LedgerDivergesFromCommitment` 274) honour that. `verify_history_chain` runs after the grant-blob loop, owner blob, owner-write-blob and ascent link — i.e. after up to `1024 + 3` entropy draws and HPKE seals. Move the call to just after line 277 (`let scope_id = identity.scope_id;`). This does not shift the entropy stream on the success path, because the check draws no entropy — confirmed, `verify_history_chain` takes no `E: Entropy` and calls no clock/RNG. Under item 1's truncation this concern disappears entirely.

---

### 4. [SECURITY] P3 — the sweep lost its self-heal, so an over-bound link set is now sticky

Old code: `keep = MAX_RETAINED_HISTORY_LINKS - usize::from(seeds.prev.is_some())`, so a **sweep** pruned to 64. New code: `None => 0`, no prune. Answering the brief: the set cannot *grow* (a sweep appends nothing) and cannot exceed the encode bound (input came off a decoded section, ≤ 256), so a >256 set cannot brick convergence. But a set of 65..256 — authorable today by a write-grantee, per item 1 — used to be trimmed by the next sweep and now is not, so the "reader-CPU amplifier" the 256 bound exists to cap becomes permanent until a rotation trims it. With item 1's fix a rotation does trim it; with the current hard error, nothing ever does. Worth stating in `blueprint/core.md:143-148`: the sweep neither grows **nor shrinks** the set.

---

### 5. [SECURITY] P4 — cheap hardening: the walk does not require epochs to decrease

The codec sees `SignedSealed { sealed, signature, unknown }` where `sealed` is `nonce || ciphertext || tag`. A link's epoch exists only in the **untransmitted AAD** and **inside the ciphertext** — both need `structure_key(override_seed(epoch))`, which `crates/core` does not have. Nothing unwalkable is published — no reader could walk past that break either — so the fail-closed property is preserved while the attacker loses the ability to block their own removal. One precision I put in the thread rather than overstate: the blast radius is *generator reproducibility*, not a wrong frozen contract. Those bytes are opaque filler in a **reject** vector — its job is to fire `too-many-structures`, which it does at any width. It would have shown up as a red CI leg on a 32-bit host, not a bad KAT.

A check at `section.rs#L352-358`/`#L376-392` could only inspect opaque bytes: it would look like enforcement and validate nothing. Rule-8 symmetry still holds for what the codec *can* see (count bounds, duplicate-`sealed`), which are release-active on both sides.

Enforced instead in `reseal.rs` on the rotation path, the one place a key into the chain exists.

**The part worth your attention:** my first cut did exactly what CodeRabbit asked — `Err` on a chain that won't walk — and **that was a denial-of-revocation vector.** Both review gates caught it independently. ---
name: feedback-never-apply-review-suggestions-literally
description: "A CodeRabbit/Greptile suggestion is a symptom report, not a spec — applying it literally has twice introduced a worse bug"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

Never hand a CodeRabbit or Greptile suggestion to a sub-agent as the specification for the fix.
Treat the finding as a symptom report: verify the underlying problem is real, then decide the remedy
against the threat model. Brief resolve-agents to triage and push back, never to "apply the
suggested diff".

Two instances in one session (2026-08-04), both caught only because the agent re-ran the review
gates on its *own* fix:

- **PR #1049** — CodeRabbit asked for `Err` on a history-link chain that will not walk. That is a
  **denial-of-revocation vector**: the adoption gate authenticates each link's signature but nothing
  about their order, so a committed write-grantee can publish an adopted root with reordered links,
  and the owner's revocation rotation then fails closed *permanently* — non-retryable on the cascade
  path, leaving a revocation half-applied. Correct remedy was to **truncate to the walkable suffix**:
  nothing unwalkable is published, fail-closed holds, the attacker cannot block their own removal.
- **PR #1046** — CodeRabbit asked for durable in-doubt publish state. That only moves the failure
  window; any single durable write has a gap after the network ack.

**Why:** the reviewer sees a local invariant violation, not the adversary model. The dangerous shape
is a suggestion that converts a currently-tolerated input into a hard failure on a path an attacker
can reach — availability/DoS risk introduced in the name of strictness. Also watch for a suggestion
naming a layer that structurally *cannot* enforce the invariant (e.g. asking the `crates/core` codec
to validate epoch ordering it cannot decrypt) — implementing it there yields a check that looks like
enforcement and validates nothing.

**How to apply:** for every finding ask (1) is the underlying defect real, (2) what does the proposed
remedy do to availability and to the adversary's options, (3) is the named layer able to check this
at all. Partial enforcement plus an explicitly stated residual beats a false guarantee. See
[[project-coderabbit-false-positive-classes]] for the separate class of findings that are simply
wrong on the mechanism.

input.content:
---
name: project-coderabbit-verdict-two-surfaces
description: "CodeRabbit puts a clean verdict in the status comment but findings in a submitted review body — poll both surfaces"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

A CodeRabbit verdict lands on one of **two** surfaces depending on the outcome, so polling only one
gives a wrong answer half the time. Observed across four PRs on 2026-08-04:

- **Clean** → `"No actionable comments were generated in the recent review. 🎉"` appears in the
  **issue status comment** (`issues/N/comments`), and `pulls/N/reviews` has **no** review with a
  non-empty body. Seen on #1036 and #1042.
- **Findings** → `"Actionable comments posted: N"` appears in a **submitted review body**
  (`pulls/N/reviews[].body`), and the status comment may never update. Seen on #1046 and #1049.

Polling only the status comment made a #1046 watcher report "still waiting" indefinitely while the
review had been sitting in the review body for 20+ minutes.

Two further traps:

- **Thread replies create `len=0` review events.** Counting `pulls/N/reviews | length` after an agent
  replies to and resolves threads shows several "reviews" that are not reviews. Filter to
  `select((.body|length)>0)` before concluding anything about rate-limit timing.
- A genuine review pass carries a **`Run ID`**, `Review profile`, and an `Estimated code review
  effort` line. Their absence means walkthrough-only or skipped, not reviewed — see
  [[project-coderabbit-walkthrough-vs-review-pass]].

**How to apply:** poll `pulls/N/reviews[].body` (non-empty only) **and** the coderabbit status
comment, matching either `Actionable comments posted: [0-9]+` or `No actionable comments were
generated`. Also: a script gating on `gh pr checks` must distinguish a network error from a red
check — an unreachable-API error line counted as a failing check once caused a false ABORT that
skipped a flip.

_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Reject whitespace-only configuration values.**

Truthy whitespace passes `missingDeployEnv` and `loginEnv`. A staging or production build can pass with a blank API URL, client ID, or verifier and then fail during engine startup or login. Whitespace also configures `acceleratorBaseUrl` instead of leaving reads dormant.

- `apps/web/src/engine/config.ts#L81-L103`: Treat values with `value.trim().length === 0` as missing. Make `loginEnv` use the same nonblank check.
- `apps/web/src/engine/config.ts#L72-L76`: Trim `VITE_READ_ACCELERATOR_URL` and convert a blank result to `undefined`.
- `apps/web/src/engine/config.test.ts#L61-L118`: Add runtime assertions for whitespace-only accelerator, API URL, client ID, and verifier values.




As per path instructions, “Focus on test coverage, edge cases, and test quality.”

=== FINDING 2 (claim after analysis) ===
</details>

**Reject JSON `null` before dispatching.**

`JSON.parse('null') as Fields` returns `null`, but `field()` treats `dto` as an object and throws when reading `publicKey`. That leaves the mock request unresolved at `/auth/challenge` or `/auth/login`.

Return `{}` unless the parsed value is a non-null object, and add a runtime test that posts `null` and expects HTTP 400.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
 function parse(body: Buffer): Fields {
   try {
-    return JSON.parse(body.toString('utf8')) as Fields;
+    const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(body.toString('utf8'));
+    return parsed !== null && typeof parsed === 'object' ? (parsed as Fields) : {};
   } catch {
     return {};
   }

**No hard technical constraint** — all six pairwise merges are clean and the combined tree compiles and tests green. But there are four soft ones worth respecting.

## Recommended order

**1. #1042** — the cleanest thing you have. Reviewed clean, and crucially **zero post-review commits**: both its commits predate the review, so what CodeRabbit saw is exactly what merges.

**2. #1049** — on current main, but see the caveat below.

**3. #1035** — **set `VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER` before this one**, or your staging build goes red at the new gate.

**4. #1039** — still needs its review (~21:26Z) plus your blueprint sign-off.

## The four things that actually matter

**#1042 and #1039 are 2 commits behind main.** Their CI ran against `3c08517d3`; main is `131d201db`. Both merge clean and I've verified the combined tree, but their green checkmarks don't reflect the current base. Rebase or re-run CI before merging either. #1049 and #1035 were both rebased and are current.

**#1049 and #1035 carry unreviewed fix commits.** That's the normal resolve-then-merge flow, but it's worth naming for #1049 specifically: its fix wasn't a tweak, it was a **design change on a trust boundary** — `Err` on an unwalkable chain became truncate-to-walkable-suffix, precisely because the reviewed-and-approved suggestion was a DoS vector. CodeRabbit never saw that redesign. The agent re-ran all three gates on it, and I verified it compiles and tests, but if you want any PR re-reviewed after merge-time changes, that's the one.

**#1035 and #1039 both touch `packages/client/test/browser/`** — `mockAuth.ts`/`engine.spec.ts` versus `leadership.spec.ts`/`leadership.ts`. Different files, and both merge clean. But **my verification never ran the Client Browser Suite on the combined tree** — it needs a built wasm `pkg`, so I can only confirm Rust and unit-level TS. Whichever of those two merges second, watch that job rather than assuming it carries over.

**The two human gates are merge-time, not review-time**, so they don't constrain ordering beyond #1035 and #1039 being last.

A fresh combined verification with the latest fix commits is running — my previous run predated #1035's rebase, so I'd rather re-confirm than quote a stale number at you.

**Validate the request payload, not only `type` and `requestId`.**

> The doc block at line 276-277 states that anything off-shape is dropped. `serve` validates `type` and `requestId` but not the payload.

This is the sharpest of the four and it is squarely in your PR's own security story: you moved commands and uploads onto the private `MessagePort` precisely so they stop crossing an origin-wide channel. A port message is still attacker-adjacent input — a compromised or buggy follower can send anything — and your own doc block promises off-shape messages are dropped while the code does not check the payload. Doc-says-X-code-does-Y on a trust boundary is exactly what the review gates exist to catch.

CodeRabbit's suggestion switches on `message.type` and narrows each payload (`typeof read?.kind !== 'string'`, etc.). Verify the shape set against your actual `PortRequest` union rather than transcribing the snippet — and make sure a rejected message is *dropped*, not thrown on, so a malformed request cannot wedge the relay or leave the sender hanging.

## Finding 4 — `packages/client/src/testkit.ts:470` — 🟡 Minor, but conceptually important

**Model transfer lists in `FakeEngineWorker.postMessage()`.**

> `LocalTransport.pushChunk()` posts `{ type: 'pushChunk', id, handle, chunk }, [chunk]`; `FakeEngineWorker.postMessage()` records the original message and leaves `chunk` readable. Tests cannot detect that `LocalTransport` moved the upload chunk.

Rated Minor, but weigh it higher than that: **your test double cannot observe the property this PR exists to establish.** #983 is about transferring buffers rather than cloning them; a fake that leaves the chunk readable will pass whether or not the transfer actually happens. Accept the transfer list and `structuredClone(message, { transfer })` before recording, so a regression that reverts to cloning fails a test.

## Finding 1 — `blueprint/web-client.md:95-109` — 🟡 Minor

**Stale focus-hint statement in the same section.** The section still claims focused followers' refresh hints ride the `BroadcastChannel`, which your `cb:portFocus` / `BroadcastTransport.reportFocus` change made false. Conventional Commits, no parentheses in the subject. `git commit` may hang on 1Password SSH signing — background Bash call with a `timeout` guard, never `--no-gpg-sign`. Keep the PR a DRAFT.

skills.content:
# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:
1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.
2. Briefly confirm: what's scheduled, the cron expression, the human-readable cadence, that recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days, and that the user can cancel sooner with CronDelete (include the job ID). Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.
3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.

## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)

The user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.

1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.
2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.
3. **Briefly confirm**: that you're self-pacing, whether a Monitor is the primary wake signal, that you ran the task now, and what fallback delay you're about to pick. Write this as text *before* calling ScheduleWakeup — the turn ends as soon as that tool returns.
4. **Then, as the last action of this turn, decide whether the loop continues.** If the task needs another iteration, call ScheduleWakeup with:
   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks more frequent than the task needs are pure overhead). Without a Monitor this is the cadence — pick based on what you observed. Read the tool's own description for cache-aware delay guidance.
   - `reason`: one short sentence on why you picked that delay.
   - `prompt`: the full original /loop input verbatim, prefixed with `/loop ` so the next firing re-enters this skill and continues the loop. For example, if the user typed `/loop check the deploy`, pass `/loop check the deploy` as the prompt.
   If it doesn't need another iteration, stop instead (step 6) — re-arming is a per-turn choice, not a default.
5. **If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`** rather than this prompt: handle the event in the context of the loop task, then make the same decision. If the loop should continue, call ScheduleWakeup again with the same `prompt` and the same 1200–1800s `delaySeconds` from step 4 (the Monitor remains the wake signal; the new wakeup is only the fallback heartbeat). If the event means the work is finished, stop (step 6).
6. **To stop the loop** — the task is complete, further iterations can't make progress, or the user asked you to stop — call ScheduleWakeup with `stop: true` (no other fields) and TaskStop any Monitor you armed (use TaskList to find the task ID if it is no longer in context). Stopping is the loop's normal ending — the user can restart it anytime with /loop. Before you stop, send a one-line outcome via PushNotification — the user may be away and waiting to hear it's done. Skip this if you're stopping because the user just told you to; they're already here.

## Input

Manage the CodeRabbit review queue for FSM1/cipher-box while the user is AFK. #1021 was flipped ready at 05:05Z — this is the LAST PR in the queue. Check whether its review posted: look at `pulls/1021/reviews` for a submitted review AND the review body for "Actionable comments posted: N" or "No actionable comments were generated"; CodeRabbit edits ONE status comment in place, so re-read before concluding, and re-flip if it was walkthrough-only or rate-limited. If the review lands with findings, re-draft #1021 IMMEDIATELY, then either fix a single small finding directly or delegate a larger set to a sub-agent that triages rather than blindly applying suggestions. #1022 is MERGED; #1024, #1023 and #1027 are reviewed with fixes applied and await the user's merge decision — do NOT re-flip any of them. Once #1021's findings are resolved the queue is COMPLETE: report a final summary of all five PRs, the issues they close, the outstanding decisions for the user, and then STOP the loop via ScheduleWakeup stop:true after sending a PushNotification. Never merge anything.

build-web:
    name: Build Web App
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      # apps/web compiles crates/wasm into the engine artifact it bundles.
      - name: Add wasm target
        run: rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@0ebf47130e4866e96fce0953f49152a61190b271 # v6.0.9

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: 'package.json'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      # wasm-bindgen-cli generates the engine glue and must match the locked
      # wasm-bindgen version exactly (a schema mismatch fails the run).
      - name: Install wasm-bindgen-cli (matching Cargo.lock)
        run: |
          WB_VERSION=$(grep -A1 '^name = "wasm-bindgen"$' Cargo.lock | grep '^version' | head -1 | sed 's/.*"\(.*\)".*/\1/')
          echo "wasm-bindgen ${WB_VERSION}"
          cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version "${WB_VERSION}" --locked

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # Kept separate from the bundle step so the staging secrets below never
      # enter the environment of a cargo build script.
      - name: Build the engine WASM artifact
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build:wasm

      - name: Build web app with staging env vars
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build:bundle
        env:
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_API_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_API_URL }}
          VITE_ENVIRONMENT: staging
          VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_FARO_URL: ${{ vars.VITE_FARO_URL }}
          GRAFANA_FARO_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_FARO_API_KEY }}
          GRAFANA_STACK_ID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_STACK_ID }}

      - name: Upload web dist as artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: web-dist
          path: apps/web/dist/
          retention-days: 1

  create-desktop-release:
    name: Create Desktop Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:

content.text:
**One thing: the `VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER` Actions variable doesn't exist at any scope.** I checked repo, `staging` env, and `staging-approval` — it's in none of them.

**Why it blocks the merge.** #1035 adds `deployEnvGate()` to `apps/web/vite.config.ts`, which throws when `missingDeployEnv()` is non-empty, and that only fires for `staging`/`production`. `deploy-staging.yml`'s `build-web` sets `VITE_ENVIRONMENT: staging`, so the first push to main after merging fails the "Build web app with staging env vars" step. That's the gate working as designed — it converts today's silent breakage (main's `coreKit.ts:88` already throws at runtime on the unset verifier) into a red build. But it goes red on the merge commit unless the variable exists first.

I checked the other two `DEPLOY_ENV` entries so this isn't a partial answer: `VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID` resolves (set at both repo and staging-env scope) and `STAGING_API_URL` → `VITE_API_URL` resolves at staging-env scope. The verifier is the only gap.

**Set it at repo scope, not environment scope.** Every staging build job (`build-web`, the three `build-desktop-*`, and all of `desktop-staging-release.yml`) declares `environment: staging`, which sees repo variables too — but `web-e2e.yml` declares no environment, and #1035 wires the verifier into both its build step and the generated `apps/web/.env`. An env-scoped variable would silently miss it. web-e2e isn't gate-blocked either way (it builds with `VITE_ENVIRONMENT` unset → `local` → exempt, and logs in via the `TEST_LOGIN_SECRET` bypass rather than Core Kit), but repo scope avoids an empty value there.

**Value: `cipherbox-identity`.** v1 hardcodes it at `apps/web/src/lib/web3auth/hooks.ts:154`, `docs/AUTHENTICATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §2.1 documents it as the custom verifier registered with Web3Auth, and the API signs with `kid: cipherbox-identity-1`. Staging is DEVNET on the same client ID as v1, so it should carry over unchanged.

Worth a dashboard confirm before you set it, though — your own comment in `config.ts` makes the point that a wrong verifier picks a different identity over an empty vault, and that failure is silent rather than red.

```
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh variable set VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER --body cipherbox-identity --repo FSM1/cipher-box
```

Say the word and I'll run it — I've held off because it's a repo settings change with a security-relevant value, not something to do on inference.

Separately: #1035 is now 1 behind main after the #1049 merge. I'll rebase it and #1039 unless #1039 is mid-review again.

---
name: project-staging-build-vars-live-at-environment-scope
description: CipherBox staging deploy vars live at the `staging` GitHub environment scope, not repo scope — but web-e2e declares no environment and only sees repo scope
metadata:
  type: project
---

`FSM1/cipher-box` splits Actions variables across two scopes, and `gh variable list` (repo scope)
shows only 5 of them — it is NOT the full picture.

- **`staging` environment scope (15 vars)** — `STAGING_API_URL`, `STAGING_HOST`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`,
  `CLOUDFLARE_*`, `GRAFANA_*`, `PHALA_TEE_WORKER_URL`, … Every staging build job
  (`deploy-staging.yml` `build-web` + `build-desktop-{macos,windows,linux}`, and all of
  `desktop-staging-release.yml`) declares `environment: staging`, so it sees repo vars *and* these.
- **Repo scope (5 vars)** — `VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER`, `GRAFANA_DS_*`,
  `GRAFANA_URL`, `RELEASE_BOT_APP_ID`. There is no org-level variable set (404).
- **`web-e2e.yml` declares NO `environment:`** — so it sees repo scope ONLY. A `VITE_*` build
  variable that web-e2e needs must be set at **repo** scope or it silently reads empty.

**Why to check this before merging a build-time env gate:** `apps/web/vite.config.ts`'s
`deployEnvGate()` throws when `missingDeployEnv()` is non-empty, and that fires only for
`VITE_ENVIRONMENT` of `staging`/`production`. An unset variable is a red staging deploy on the merge
commit, not a runtime bug. Verify by running the real build both ways before merging:

```
VITE_ENVIRONMENT=staging VITE_API_URL=… VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID=… \
  pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build:bundle
```

Unset → `Error: a staging build cannot log in without <NAME>`; set → exit 0. The error names every
missing variable, so one negative-control run also proves the *others* resolve.

`VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER = cipherbox-identity` was set at repo scope 2026-08-04 to unblock #1035.
That value is v1's hardcoded verifier (`docs/AUTHENTICATION_ARCHITECTURE.md` §2.1; the API signs its
JWT with `kid: cipherbox-identity-1`), and staging is DEVNET on the same client ID.

See [[project-v1-staging-only-devnet.md]] and [[project-ci-excludes-web-unit-tests]].

content.text:
**Because `main` has no branch protection at all.** Nothing is enforcing those checks — the merge button is just showing you the status, not gating on it.

```
GET repos/FSM1/cipher-box/branches/main/protection  →  404 "Branch not protected"
```

The only ruleset on the repo targets **tags**, not branches: `refs/tags/v*` with `deletion` / `non_fast_forward` / `update` rules — that's the v1-freeze / release-tag immutability, and it says nothing about `main`.

So on `main` right now there is no required-status-checks list, no required review, and no push restriction. `AGENTS.md`'s "NEVER push directly to `main` — all changes must go through feature branches and PRs" is convention enforced by us, not by GitHub. A stray `git push origin main` would land.

Two practical consequences worth knowing:

**"20 successful checks" is not the same as "the checks that matter passed."** With no required list, GitHub reports whatever happened to report. The two still running are `Cargo Check & Test` on Linux and Windows — the Rust compile-and-test legs, i.e. the ones most likely to catch a semantic merge conflict. Everything green so far is API/build/lint. That's exactly the ordering where the button is least informative.

**`Desktop Build` shows "Skipped", which is by design** — that's the `if: always()` result gate we set up so the matrix legs don't deadlock. It's not a check that failed to run.

If you want the gate real, a minimal ruleset on `main` requiring `CI / Cargo Check & Test (Linux)`, `(Windows)`, `CI / Build`, and `CI / Test` would do it, plus `non_fast_forward`. Say the word and I'll write it — though note it would apply to you too, and release-please's bot pushes to `main` directly, so it needs a bypass actor or the release train breaks.

For this PR specifically: I verified the equivalent locally before pushing (`cargo check --workspace --all-targets` 0, 988 Rust tests, wasm32 clean), so the two pending legs should be confirmation rather than news — but they haven't confirmed it yet. I'd let them finish.

# v2 release management (blueprint/deploy.md in FSM1/cipher-box-next): one
# product version vX.Y.Z, single-component release-please, no per-package
# versioning. DORMANT during the v2 build — dispatch-only so no release PRs
# accumulate over the demolition. Re-engage by restoring the push->main
# trigger when the first v2.0.0 release candidate is ready.
name: Release Please

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  release-please:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      releases_created: ${{ steps.release.outputs.releases_created }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ vars.RELEASE_BOT_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_BOT_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - uses: googleapis/release-please-action@45996ed1f6d02564a971a2fa1b5860e934307cf7 # v5.0.0
        id: release
        with:
          config-file: release-please-config.json
          manifest-file: .release-please-manifest.json
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

      - name: Release summary
        if: steps.release.outputs.releases_created == 'true'
        env:
          RELEASES_OUTPUT: ${{ toJSON(steps.release.outputs) }}
        run: |
          echo "## Releases Created" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          echo '```json' >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

<result>All four CodeRabbit findings resolved. PR #1039 is still a **draft**, rebased on `18dec88af`, pushed as `63879ad2a`.

## Per finding

**Finding 3 (Major) — payload validation. Accepted, but I did not take the suggested diff.** I reproduced first with a table-driven test, and the defect was both real and broader than described:

- `cb:portWrite` with no `write` — confirmed exactly as reported: `TypeError` escaping `serveWrite` → `serve` → `onPortMessage` → the listener. No correlated failure, no wipe, sender hangs forever.
- `cb:portRead` with no `read` — **does not throw.** `readValue` falls out of a switch exhaustive over the *valid* union, so the relay answered `{ok: true, result: undefined}`. A fail-open, not a hang — CodeRabbit's reasoning ("answerPort catches it") was wrong about the mechanism.
- `cb:portFocus` with a string `node` — also no throw; `hex()` iterates the string and `'n'.toString(16)` ignores the radix, silently keying the focus registry on nonsense.
- `cb:portStream` was already safe (async, so the deref becomes a catchable rejection).

**The suggested diff would have regressed three of four arms.** It returns `false`, which means *drop* — and dropping a correlated request is a hang, because `CorrelatedTransport`'s pending map has no timeout. Read/stream/command already settle an error today.

**What landed:** off-shape input that names an answerable request (numeric `requestId`, named port) gets a correlated `ok:false` with a transport-level `malformed()` error — now including an unknown `type`, which the old code dropped and which is the case cross-build skew actually hits. Input that *cannot* be answered (unnamed port, no `requestId`, uncorrelated focus, non-object payload) is dropped and any chunk wiped. Handler switches carry an `unknownKind(_: never)` bound; I verified adding a variant to `WireRead`, `WireWrite` and `WireStream` each produces `TS2322 ... not assignable to type 'never'`.

**Re-running the crypto/privacy gate on my own fix caught that it was incomplete, in the same class** — worth noting given the coordinator's warning:
- `serveWrite`'s *inner* switch had the identical fail-open on an **owned** handle: `{kind:'bogus', handle:<owned>}` acked `ok:true` for a step never run — silent byte loss on a streamed upload.
- The chunk wipe was keyed off the declared `kind`, so a well-formed `commitWrite` merely carrying a buffer left plaintext live in the leader's heap. Now one wipe in a `finally`, keyed off the buffer, covering every kind and outcome.
- `streamStep`'s tail treated any leftover kind as `readStream`, passing `undefined` offset/length to the engine.

**Finding 4 — transfer list. Accepted, and I agree it is above Minor.** Proved it is load-bearing: added an assertion that the leader path detaches the chunk, then neutered `LocalTransport.pushChunk`'s transfer list — the test fails with `expected 4 to be +0`. Restored, green.

**Finding 1 — stale blueprint sentence. Accepted**, took CodeRabbit's wording. `npx markdownlint-cli2 blueprint/web-client.md` → 0 issues.

**Finding 2 — timing margin. Accepted**, `10_000`. Confirmed non-vacuous by deleting the `clientId === null` guard in `sweepLiveness`: the test fails with `cb:portPing` + `cb:portClosed`.

## Gates

`pnpm typecheck` clean, `pnpm lint` clean, `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/client test` **338 passing** (was 323), browser-suite typecheck clean apart from the pre-existing missing-wasm-`pkg` errors. Also ran a simplify pass on the grown delta and folded it in — three copies of the exhaustiveness ceremony collapsed to one helper, two `wipe*` helpers to one, a near-clone test merged, and the restated comments cut.

## One thing outside my boundary

Filed **#1051** (dependency edge → #983): `buildCommand` in `packages/client/src/worker/commandCodec.ts` has no `default` arm and lets wasm-bindgen coerce wrong-typed fields — `{kind:'rename', newName: 12345}` renames a node to `"12345"`. The relay now rejects a payload that is not a command *shape*, but field validation is the codec's job and it does not do it. `worker/**` belongs to #1035, so I did not touch it.

Still open from the first pass: #1037 (worker-side chunk zeroize), #1038 (presence-lock liveness).</result>

content.text:
**Classic protection is back on `main`.** No branch protection existed at all — the only ruleset targeted `refs/tags/v*`, so nothing gated the merge button.

**What I set**

- **19 required status checks** — `Lint`, `Typecheck`, `Test`, `Build`, `Web Bundle`, `API Unit`, `API Integration (real Postgres)`, `Migration Drift`, `OpenAPI Freshness`, all three `Cargo Check & Test` legs, `Engine Tests`, `Core KATs (native + WASM)`, `Client Browser Suite`, `Contract Suite Result`, `Desktop Build Result`, `lint-pr-title`, `zizmor static audit`
- **`enforce_admins: true`** — without it this is decorative, since you're the only human with write access. It also blocks direct `git push origin main`, which makes AGENTS.md's "never push directly to main" real rather than honor-system.
- **Force-pushes and deletions blocked.**
- **No required reviews**, deliberately — see below.
- **`strict: false`** — branches don't have to be up-to-date with main. You merged #1042 un-rebased on purpose, so requiring it would have fought your workflow.

**Two traps I steered around**

I required `Contract Suite Result` and `Desktop Build Result`, not `Contract Suite` and `Desktop Build`. `desktop-build` is a matrix (`runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}`), and when its path filter skips it the context name changes shape — requiring the legs deadlocks every doc-only PR. The `if: always()` gates exist for exactly this; the comment at `ci.yml:289` even says so.

I did **not** enable required reviews. You're the sole maintainer and GitHub won't let you approve your own PR, so any non-zero approval count would have locked you out of merging entirely.

**Verified rather than assumed:** I diffed all 19 required contexts against the check runs actually produced on #1035's head — zero required-but-absent. A typo there is a permanently unmergeable repo. `release-please.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only during the v2 build and the last 200 commits on main are all PR squashes, so there's no bot pushing directly that this would break.

Two knobs I left off that you may want: `required_conversation_resolution` (would force CodeRabbit threads resolved before merge — fits your flow, but bot threads occasionally can't be resolved) and `required_linear_history`.

**Separately — #1039's agent finished** and pushed `63879ad2a`, so it's now one behind main and needs a rebase. Worth your attention: it rejected CodeRabbit's suggested diff for the Major finding and was right to. The suggestion returned `false`, which means *drop*, and `CorrelatedTransport`'s pending map has no timeout — so dropping a correlated request hangs the sender forever. It also found the finding was understated: two more arms were failing *open* rather than throwing, including one that acked `ok:true` for a write step never run. Client tests 338 passing, up from 323.

+## `main` branch protection RESTORED 2026-08-05
+`main` had **no protection at all** — `GET branches/main/protection` → 404, and the sole ruleset
+targets `refs/tags/v*` (`deletion`/`non_fast_forward`/`update`, the freeze-tag immutability). The
+merge button was reporting check status, not gating on it.
+Applied classic protection: 19 required contexts, `enforce_admins: true`, force-push and deletion
+blocked, `strict: false` (branches need not be up to date — #1042 was merged un-rebased on purpose),
+`required_pull_request_reviews: null`.
+Three decisions worth keeping:
+- **No required reviews.** Solo maintainer; GitHub forbids self-approval, so any non-zero approval
+  count locks the repo. CodeRabbit approval is not dependable enough to be the only path to merge.
+- **Required `Contract Suite Result` / `Desktop Build Result`, never the underlying jobs.**
+  `desktop-build` is a matrix (`runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}`); when its path filter skips it the
+  context name changes shape, so requiring the legs deadlocks every doc-only PR. `ci.yml:289`
+  documents the `if: always()` gate as existing for exactly this.
+- **`enforce_admins: true`** — otherwise decorative for the only human with write access. Also
+  blocks direct `git push origin main`, making the AGENTS.md rule enforced rather than honor-system.
+Verified by set-diffing all 19 required contexts against the check runs actually produced on
+#1035's head: zero required-but-absent. A typo there is a permanently unmergeable repo.
+Safe to apply now because `release-please.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only during the v2 build and
+the last 200 commits on `main` are all PR squashes — no bot pushes directly.
+Left OFF, available if wanted: `required_conversation_resolution`, `required_linear_history`.
All four remaining verified against new main 2026-08-04: `merge-tree` CLEAN individually, and the
combined four-way merge is green — native **1201 passed / 0 failed**, `wasm32-unknown-unknown`
clean, `wasm32-wasip1` **327 passed / 0 failed**.
